--- title: "SNP-slice analysis using snp.slicer" output: html_document --- ## Introduction This tutorial estimates complexity of infection (COI) and multi-locus allele frequencies with SNP-Slice. The algorithm is from [Ju, Liu, and He (2024)](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae344). Their [original repository](https://github.com/nianqiaoju/snp-slice) is a set of scripts rather than an R package, and those scripts are difficult to install and run. The example uses [`snp.slicer`](https://github.com/plasmogenepi/snp.slicer), an R package that implements that algorithm. Install it with the [installation instructions](installation.Rmd) before running the code below. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(tidyverse) library(here) library(vcfR) library(snp.slicer) library(kableExtra) ``` ::: ## The data The data are the simulated sanger 100-SNP barcode: 100 polyclonal infections, 50 drawn from Bangladesh and 50 from Ghana. The file is described with the other [SNP barcode data](../../website_docs/data_snps.qmd). `snp_slice()` reads a data frame with one row per observed allele: - `specimen_id`: sample name - `target_id`: SNP name - `target_value`: allele code - `target_count`: read count for that allele The VCF stores allelic depth in `FORMAT/AD`. The two numbers are the reference-allele count and the alternate-allele count. Those become `target_value` `"0"` and `"1"`. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} vcf_data <- read.vcfR( here::here("data/snp_barcode/SpotMalariapfPanel_simData_sanger100.vcf.gz") ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` Scanning file to determine attributes. File attributes: meta lines: 76 header_line: 77 variant count: 100 column count: 109 Meta line 76 read in. All meta lines processed. gt matrix initialized. Character matrix gt created. Character matrix gt rows: 100 Character matrix gt cols: 109 skip: 0 nrows: 100 row_num: 0 Processed variant: 100 All variants processed ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} counts_raw <- t(vcfR::extract.gt(vcf_data, element = "AD")) read0 <- vcfR::masplit( counts_raw, record = 1, sort = FALSE, decreasing = FALSE ) |> as.data.frame() |> rownames_to_column(var = "specimen_id") |> pivot_longer( cols = -specimen_id, names_to = "target_id", values_to = "target_count" ) |> mutate(target_value = "0") read1 <- vcfR::masplit( counts_raw, record = 2, sort = FALSE, decreasing = FALSE ) |> as.data.frame() |> rownames_to_column(var = "specimen_id") |> pivot_longer( cols = -specimen_id, names_to = "target_id", values_to = "target_count" ) |> mutate(target_value = "1") snpslice_data <- rbind(read0, read1) |> arrange(specimen_id, target_id) snpslice_data |> slice_head(n = 6) |> kable() |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
specimen_id target_id target_count target_value
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_145515 7569 0
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_145515 1977 1
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_179347 1971 0
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_179347 8154 1
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_180554 8998 0
Bangladesh-01 Pf3D7_01_v3_180554 1973 1
````` ::: ::: ## Run SNP-Slice `snp_slice()` fits the model by MCMC. The default keeps 10,000 samples after burn-in. This page uses `n_sample = 100` so the example finishes quickly. Read the summary it prints: a short chain often has not converged, and those estimates are only there to show the output. Use the default `n_sample` for an analysis you will interpret. `model = "negative_binomial"` uses the read counts. `seed` makes this short run repeatable. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} run <- snp_slice( snpslice_data, model = "negative_binomial", n_sample = 100, seed = 1, verbose = FALSE ) summary(run) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` SNP-Slice Results Summary ======================== Model: negative_binomial Data dimensions: 100 hosts x 100 SNPs Data type: read_counts Results: - Number of strains identified: 121 - Number of hosts: 100 - Multiplicity of infection (MOI): - Mean MOI: 15.45 - Median MOI: 15 - Range: 11 - 24 - Single infections: 0 ( 0 %) - Mixed infections: 100 ( 100 %) Convergence: - Iterations run: 150 - Samples retained (post-burn-in): 100 - Gap Converged: No - Final log posterior: -5801308 - MAP log posterior: -5801266 - Final k*: 121 - MAP k*: 121 ``` ::: ::: ## Multi-locus allele frequencies `calculate_allele_frequencies()` treats a set of SNPs as one haplotype. Each row is one haplotype across the SNPs you name, in that order. In the allele string, `0` is the reference allele and `1` is the alternate allele. `frequency` is the proportion of inferred parasite strains that carry that haplotype, and the frequencies sum to 1. The default estimate is the final sample of the chain. Set `estimate = "posterior"` and rerun `snp_slice()` with `store_mcmc = TRUE` when you want a credible interval. That needs a longer chain than the one above. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} allele_freqs <- calculate_allele_frequencies( run, c("Pf3D7_01_v3_145515", "Pf3D7_01_v3_179347", "Pf3D7_01_v3_180554") ) allele_freqs |> kable(digits = 3) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
allele frequency count total_parasites
1 0|1|0 0.423 654 1545
2 1|1|0 0.185 286 1545
5 0|1|1 0.129 200 1545
4 1|0|0 0.063 98 1545
8 1|0|1 0.060 92 1545
3 0|0|0 0.052 80 1545
6 1|1|1 0.047 73 1545
7 0|0|1 0.040 62 1545
````` ::: ::: ## Complexity of infection `calculate_individual_coi()` returns one COI per specimen from that same final sample. The uncertainty columns are empty for a point estimate. They are filled when `estimate = "posterior"` and the MCMC samples were stored. ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} coi <- calculate_individual_coi(run) coi |> slice_head(n = 6) |> kable(digits = 2) |> kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed")) ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} `````{=html}
host_index host_id coi_estimate coi_sd coi_lower coi_upper
1 Bangladesh-01 13 NA NA NA
2 Bangladesh-02 13 NA NA NA
3 Bangladesh-03 12 NA NA NA
4 Bangladesh-04 14 NA NA NA
5 Bangladesh-05 18 NA NA NA
6 Bangladesh-06 13 NA NA NA
````` ::: ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} ggplot(coi, aes(x = coi_estimate)) + geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "white", fill = "#325b74") + theme_linedraw() + labs(x = "COI", y = "Samples") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](analysis_files/figure-html/unnamed-chunk-6-1.png){width=672} ::: ::: ## Summary `snp.slicer` runs the SNP-Slice algorithm of Ju, Liu, and He on a table of allele read counts. This example estimated COI for each simulated infection and the frequency of haplotypes across three barcode SNPs. Cite the [Bioinformatics paper](https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btae344) for the method. The original scripts remain in [nianqiaoju/snp-slice](https://github.com/nianqiaoju/snp-slice).
